$schema_note: Canonical cross-implementation fixture for the session-name filter's fnmatch-style glob matcher (muxplex-4h9). Consumed identically by frontend/app.js's matchesNamePattern()/_globToRegExp() and muxplex.views' matches_name_pattern() (docs/API_SEMANTICS.md's `settings.session_filter` entry -- both must move together). Each case is a single (name, pattern) -> expected boolean match. Deliberately does NOT cover blank/whitespace-only/null/undefined pattern behavior ('no filter, return everything unchanged') -- that is a property of filterByNamePattern()/filter_by_name_pattern() ONE LAYER UP from the raw matcher this fixture drives, and is tested directly in test_session_filter.mjs's Group B instead.

cases.name: alpha
cases.why: exact literal match

cases.name: alpha
cases.why: exact literal, different string, no match

cases.name: alphabeta
cases.why: the pattern must match the ENTIRE name (anchored), not a substring -- this is what distinguishes glob matching from filterByQuery()'s substring semantics

cases.name: alpha-1
cases.why: trailing * matches any suffix, including non-empty

cases.name: build-log
cases.why: leading * matches any prefix

cases.name: foo-bar-baz
cases.why: * in the middle matches an interior segment

cases.name: anything-at-all
cases.why: a bare * matches every name, including one containing hyphens

cases.name: anything
cases.why: consecutive stars collapse into a single .* -- must not require two non-empty segments

cases.name: cat
cases.why: ? matches exactly one character

cases.name: cats
cases.why: ? matches exactly one character, not zero or many -- a longer name must not match

cases.name: v1
cases.why: [0-9] is a standard character-class range, one digit

cases.name: va
cases.why: 'a' is not in the [0-9] class

cases.name: vx
cases.why: [!seq] is fnmatch negation (NOT [^seq]) -- 'x' is not a digit, so it matches the negated class

cases.name: v5
cases.why: '5' IS a digit, so it must NOT match the negated class [!0-9]

cases.name: a[b
cases.why: an unterminated [ (no closing ]) is treated as a literal '[' character, not a broken class

cases.name: ab
cases.why: since the unterminated [ is literal, 'a[b' does not match 'ab' (missing the literal bracket)
fnmatch negation is ONLY '!', never '^' -- a literal leading ^ inside a class body is an ordinary member of the class (escaped so it can't be misread as regex negation), so '^' itself matches [^ab]

cases.name: c
cases.why: the class [^ab] (literal ^, a, b members, NOT negated) does not include 'c'

cases.name: ALPHA
cases.why: matching is case-insensitive: uppercase name vs lowercase pattern

cases.name: alpha
cases.why: matching is case-insensitive: lowercase name vs uppercase pattern

cases.name: foo.bar
cases.why: a literal '.' in the pattern matches a literal '.' in the name

cases.name: fooXbar
cases.why: '.' is NOT a glob wildcard (only ? and * are) -- it must be escaped to a literal regex '.', so it does not match an arbitrary character here

cases.name: a+b
cases.why: a literal '+' in the pattern matches a literal '+' -- regex metacharacters in the pattern must be escaped, not interpreted

cases.name: ab
cases.why: '+' is escaped to a literal character, not a regex quantifier -- 'ab' (no plus) must not match

cases.name: session-01
cases.why: multiple character classes compose within a single pattern

cases.name: session-1
cases.why: only one digit present where the pattern requires exactly two
